messages:
maya: Quick sync — ACME just escalated. They want a committed latency SLO for chat inference next quarter. Asking whether we should re-scope the upcoming perf sprint to prioritize latency over batching/cost work. Thoughts?
kevin: Do we have concrete numbers from ACME? e.g., p95 target and acceptable token cost increase?
sarah: ACME email said p95 < 120ms for short-chat (<=64 tokens). They said cost can rise up to ~15% if reliability and latency are met.
oliver: 120ms p95 on what model/hardware? that's pretty tight for current hosted stack. Could be doable on Dedicated with optimized kernels + KV caching but not on current stock instances.
pranav: If we prioritize latency first, flow-on work: faster kernels, smaller batch sizes, dedicate hot GPU pool for their slice. That reduces throughput/cost efficiency. RICE-wise: impact high (enterprise contract), effort high.
eva: If we use RICE calc quickly: Reach = 1 (single large customer), Impact = 8 (renewal), Confidence = 0.6, Effort = 40 engineer-weeks estimate -> score ~ (1*8*0.6)/40 = 0.12. Low absolute but context matters (strategic customer).
maya: Right — RICE numbers don't capture strategic weighting. We should add a non-quantitative multiplier for strategic customers. Also need launch criteria: p95 verified <120ms on production traffic subset, regression <1% in quality, and documented fallback to 2nd-best model if capacity spike.
kevin: Ops question: can Dedicated handle a canary for this? We could spin dedicated nodes and route ACME traffic there with a canary policy. That buys latency but costs commit.
oliver: Implementation paths: A) kernel+compiler optimizations + reserved hot path (works hostside but needs infra changes); B) route to smaller context model with distillation for ACME (affects quality); C) offer dedicated pool (higher cost, faster).
sarah: Customer preference: they want minimal API changes. So B is risky. They prefer infra+runtime changes (A) or Dedicated (C).
pranav: For sequencing, propose: 1) short spike: allocate dedicated pool for ACME as a stopgap (fastest to satisfy SLO), 2) parallel runtime perf work during sprint to reduce unit cost (longer horizon). That splits risk.
maya: I like that. Need approvals: finance for Dedicated pricing concession, sales legal for contract amendment, infra capacity to reserve GPUs. Action items: @kevin cost estimate for dedicated pool by EOD, @sarah draft contract clause, @oliver scope runtime perf epic with rough story points.
kevin: Will do cost estimate — assuming 4x A10 equivalent for HA -> rough $Xk/month. I'll post numbers here.
oliver: I'll push a minimal perf spike plan: kernel tweaks + smaller batching for ACME slice, try to preserve key batching for others. Estimate 6w to validate in staging.
sarah: Drafting contract clause now. Will propose temporary SLO addendum + opt-out if costs exceed threshold.
maya: One more governance check: product committee needs to sign off on strategic exception to roadmap. I'll add to tomorrow's meeting. If approved we shift sprint swap.
deploy-bot: Reminder: Release window locks in 48h for next sprint changes. Please comment if swap needed.
kevin: Noted — will upload numbers within 12h.
pranav: Also recommend we add a short evaluation harness for ACME traffic to measure quality regressions quickly.
eva: Agree — set up perf+quality dashboards and alerting for the canary. I can own dashboards.
maya: Thanks team. Final preference for doc: I'll synthesize decision and stakeholders, and if Product Committee approves, we'll swap sprint lanes: Batching/cost -> deferred; Latency/customer SLO -> in.
kevin: :thumbsup:
